title: Evolution of Indian Economic Planning: PC to NITI Aayog
summary: Indian planning transitioned from centralized 5-year Command Planning to NITI Aayog's cooperative federalism and strategic visioning.

blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Indian planning transitioned from centralized 5-year Command Planning to NITI Aayog's cooperative federalism and strategic visioning.

blocks.content: 🗺️ Evolution of Economic Planning in India
1. Planning Commission (March 15, 1950): Extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created by cabinet resolution. Top-down allocation of financial grants to states under Art 282.
2. Landmark 5-Year Plans: 1st Plan (Harrod-Domar agri) | 2nd Plan (Mahalanobis heavy industry) | 5th Plan (Garibi Hatao) | 12th Plan (2012-17 - Last FYP).
3. NITI Aayog (Jan 1, 2015): Think tank promoting **Cooperative Federalism** ('Bottom-up' approach). **NO power to allocate financial funds** to states!
4. Governing Council: Prime Minister (Chair) + Chief Ministers of all States + Lt. Governors of UTs.

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. Planning Commission vs. NITI Aayog Comparison Matrix
| Parameter | Planning Commission (1950–2014) | NITI Aayog (Jan 1, 2015 – Present) |
|---|---|---|
| **Nature of Body** | Extra-constitutional, non-statutory | Extra-constitutional, non-statutory policy Think Tank |
| **Planning Direction** | **Top-Down** (Center dictated plans to States) | **Bottom-Up** (States equal partners in national growth) |
| **Financial Power** | **Allocated central plan funds** to states (Art 282) | **ZERO financial allocation powers** (Ministry of Finance allocates funds) |
| **State Representation** | States represented in NDC (National Development Council) | States integral part of **Governing Council** |
| **Planning Horizon** | 5-Year Plans (12th FYP was last: 2012–17) | 15-Year Vision, 7-Year Strategy, 3-Year Action Agenda |

📖 2. Key Historical Five-Year Plans Summary
- **1st Plan (1951–56):** Harrod-Domar Model (Focus on Agriculture & Irrigation - Bhakra Nangal Dam). Target: 2.1%, Achieved: 3.6%.
- **2nd Plan (1956–61):** PC Mahalanobis Model (Focus on Rapid Industrialization & Heavy Basic Industries - Durgapur, Rourkela, Bhilai steel plants).
- **3rd Plan (1961–66):** Gadgil Yojana (Agri + Industry). Interrupted by Indo-China War (1962), Indo-Pak War (1965), and drought $ightarrow$ Led to **Plan Holiday (1966–69)**.
- **5th Plan (1974–78):** Drafted by D.D. Dhar. Focus on *Garibi Hatao* (Poverty Alleviation) and Self-Reliance.
- **12th Plan (2012–17):** Theme: *"Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth"*. Target growth: 8%.

⚖️ 3. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** NITI Aayog does NOT allocate financial resources or development grants to states! That power rests entirely with the Ministry of Finance.
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** Both Planning Commission and NITI Aayog are **non-statutory** (neither created by Constitution nor by Act of Parliament; created by Executive Resolution).

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which major structural power held by the former Planning Commission was EXCLUDED from NITI Aayog upon its creation in 2015?  
(A) Formulating long-term national policy visions  
(B) Power to allocate financial plan funds and grants to State Governments  
(C) Conducting policy evaluation studies  
(D) Interacting with state Chief Ministers in councils  
**Answer: — NITI Aayog has no fund allocation power; financial grants are handled by Finance Ministry.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** A state government requests NITI Aayog for an extra ₹500 Crore development grant for flood relief. How will NITI Aayog legally respond?  
**Resolution:** NITI Aayog will direct the request to the Ministry of Finance / Department of Expenditure, as NITI Aayog lacks statutory or executive authority to disburse funds.

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Evaluate the transition from command planning under the Planning Commission to cooperative federalism under NITI Aayog. How does NITI Aayog foster competitive federalism among Indian states?'*
🎯 Exam Angle → 🔥 HIGH — Master the distinctions between monetary policy tools (Repo vs Reverse Repo, MSF, SDF) and fiscal deficit calculation formulas.
